title: The worker writes an ack file and that ack is the delivery receipt
action: Make the delivery receipt something the worker WRITES instead of something bee infers from herdr state (D4, which narrows D1). Two files. (1) mailbox.rs. Beside `result_path` (line 67) and `result_filename` (line 88) add the round's ack path — `.bee/mailbox/<job-id>/ack-<round>.json` — plus a presence reader in the same style as the result-file readers, and extend the module header map at line 13 that lists the mailbox's files. Then `render_brief` (line 126): the brief gains a FIRST-STEP block, ahead of everything else it currently says, instructing the worker that before any other step it must write its ack file atomically — write `ack-<N>.json.tmp` then rename, the exact tmp-then-rename gesture the brief already teaches for the result file (see the existing test `render_brief_includes_the_tmp_then_rename_gesture`, line 421) — carrying a JSON object with the worker nickname, the cell id when the brief carries one, the job id, the round number, the agent's own name for itself, and a `received_at` ISO-8601 timestamp. Name the absolute path in the brief exactly as the result path is named, so a worker with no bee knowledge can follow it verbatim. Keep the brief's existing Result-form block, round numbering and schema block byte-identical apart from the new block. (2) run.rs. `deliver_pointer` — as hps-1 left it — takes its receipt from herdr's observation of the submission. Replace that receipt with the ack: delivery is confirmed when the round's ack file appears, or when the round's result file appears (an ultra-fast round that finishes before an ack is observed still counts — keep the existing `result_present()` escape and add an `ack_present()` beside it). herdr lifecycle state stops being the SUCCESS signal entirely. What stays exactly as hps-1 built it: herdr's `agent_prompt_stalled` and the `blocked` state remain the fast FAILURE detectors, ending the wait at once with their named errors. A bounded resend of the idempotent pointer while neither ack nor result has appeared is still correct — the pointer just re-points at the same brief — but it must be bounded and it must not swallow a stall or a blocked observation. Also let the ack count as a heartbeat wherever the round poll counts `log.txt` activity, so a worker that acked and then thinks for a long time is not read as dead. Tests: cover the ack path and filename, the brief carrying the first-step ack block with the tmp-then-rename gesture, delivery confirmed by an ack file, delivery still confirmed by a result file with no ack, a stall and a blocked observation still failing fast, and a bounded resend while neither file has appeared.

truths: The rendered brief tells the worker to write ack-<round>.json atomically before any other step, naming its absolute path
The ack file carries who took the job: worker nickname, cell id when present, job id, round, agent name, received_at
Delivery is confirmed by the ack file or the result file, never by a herdr lifecycle state
agent_prompt_stalled and blocked still end the wait at once

artifacts.substantive: ack path, filename, presence reader, and the brief's first-step ack block with tests; no TODO stubs
ack-or-result delivery receipt, ack counted as a heartbeat, stall and blocked failure paths untouched, with tests

key_links: the ack file also counts as a heartbeat in the round poll
prohibitions: Do not reintroduce a herdr lifecycle state as the delivery success signal
Do not drop the result_present() escape for an ultra-fast round
Do not weaken the agent_prompt_stalled or blocked fast-fail paths hps-1 added
No change to the brief's existing Result-form block, round numbering or result schema
